# woff2 / convert_woff2ttf_fuzzer

woff2's own fuzz target `convert_woff2ttf_fuzzer` ([source](source/convert_woff2ttf_fuzzer.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over woff2 (google/woff2 at fb9c3379).

woff2::ConvertWOFF2ToTTF into a WOFF2StringOut (30 MiB cap / sized from ComputeWOFF2FinalSize); the boolean result and the TTF bytes are discarded (no re-encode or checksum comparison by the harness).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against woff2 at commit fb9c3379.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing, so a statement about it says only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch woff2` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `convert_woff2ttf_fuzzer.plain` | 500,424 | `f30be9bf445f594af68583a3e1ca3538b92bc5a5ec1900f10d5b0d783509e8bf` |
| ubsan | `convert_woff2ttf_fuzzer.ubsan` | 512,688 | `76907e7e2b8ff242ba2884ffcf5b64c2a6ce6f388347149d4c18c0f1d8ad9e67` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.
